queue.goal: Turn Relay's production primitives into a durable resumable operation framework so agents invoke policy-defined workflows instead of manually conducting every GitHub, Cloudflare, Runner and QA step.
queue.acceptance: Every substantial workflow can create a stable operation_id with persisted stage/state, exact source/head/PR/check/merge/version/deployment/runtime identities, timestamps, retry/reconciliation history, blocker/waiting-for-human state and recovery/rollback state; reconnecting agents can resume from the durable receipt without reconstructing chat history; server-side recipes cover at least ship-change, publish-worker, qa-then-merge and rollback-release; ambiguous mutations reconcile by readback before retry; event/webhook updates can advance operation state without chat polling; release policy supports bounded canary/verify/promote/rollback semantics without protection bypass; operation status/history is queryable for UI; tool-surface growth stays minimal by preferring recipes/resources/contracts over one tool per step.
queue.next_action: Define and test the operation/receipt schema and transition invariants first. Reuse existing Relay source/cloud/verify primitives; do not fork their auth or safety rules.

queue.goal: Make Relay's primary product experience an interactive in-chat MCP App rather than a prose wrapper around headless tools.
queue.acceptance: ChatGPT can render compact live operation cards, project status, release/deployment state and human-QA requests directly in conversation; human-QA UI consumes the canonical Runner QA-helper contract and Visuals IDs, supports targeted questions/checklists/notes/verdicts, and can expand into a full-screen review experience without creating a parallel store; render surfaces reuse durable Relay operation receipts and existing bounded mutation tools; headless production tools remain mostly headless; UI can send bounded follow-up actions/messages, refresh state, and preserve exact artifact identity; stale artifact/evidence state is visibly invalidated; mobile/desktop layouts remain useful; picture-in-picture/persistent mini-status may be explored where supported but is not required for correctness.
queue.next_action: Begin after the durable operation receipt shape is stable enough to consume. Treat the current qa-shell design as authoritative for human review interaction; wire to it rather than redesigning it.

queue.goal: Expose Relay's MCP App dashboard as a first-class authenticated web dashboard on relay.loew.fi with parity to the in-chat state model and controls.
queue.acceptance: relay.loew.fi presents the same projects, durable operations, publication receipts, QA handoffs, release state, recovery/rollback actions and history as the MCP App without duplicating state; shared components/data adapters are reused where practical; deep links can open a specific project/operation/release/QA item; auth and mutations use Relay's existing bounded control plane; web and in-chat surfaces remain behaviorally consistent; the dashboard consumes the future shared suite shell/navigation so Relay feels like one utility with Runner and Inspector rather than a separate website.
queue.next_action: Implement after the operation framework and core MCP App view-model/components are stable; do not create a second state or approval system for web.

queue.goal: Make inspector.loew.fi the suite's dedicated visual-review dashboard, moving the visual review experience out of Runner's product surface while keeping Runner as the coordination/evidence authority.
queue.acceptance: Inspector web renders screenshots, videos, live-preview availability, targeted QA-helper questions/checklists, notes/verdicts, upload/archive/expiry state and exact operation/publication context from Runner/Relay; Runner remains authoritative for Visuals receipts, QA identity and coordination rather than duplicating those stores in Inspector; Inspector supports direct links to exact evidence/run/artifact and full-screen review; Runner dashboard links/deep-links into Inspector for visual review instead of maintaining a competing review UI once migration is complete; the design consumes the shared suite shell and feels seamless with runner.loew.fi and relay.loew.fi; migration preserves historical review/evidence identity.
queue.next_action: Start only after Runner's current operator/qa-shell design and Visuals backend contracts settle enough to consume. Treat this as a presentation migration/integration, not an evidence-authority migration.

queue.goal: Batch 1: remove hard dependencies on the old loew-inspector/loew-runner identities and make Relay source/MCP control ready for a canonical relay repo/project/runtime without changing production routing yet.
queue.acceptance: Canonical source repository references resolve lrnolivia/relay directly with no reliance on GitHub rename redirects; MCP source annotations, upload/source lifecycle logic and repository allowlists understand relay; Runner-control repository/project identity is configurable or migration-aware rather than permanently hardcoded to loew-runner; the existing live MCP remains usable throughout this batch; tests cover identity/config migration and fail closed on ambiguous control authority; no old production hostname/script is deleted or switched in this batch.
queue.next_action: Claim only after program preflight. Implement the non-destructive identity bridge and prove MCP tool/resource discovery still works before Batch 2.

queue.goal: Batch 2: import loew-runner code and history into lrnolivia/relay and establish the monorepo layout where runner and inspector are internal subsystems and night shift is a Relay feature.
queue.acceptance: Relay contains an implementation-ready monorepo layout with MCP/web apps plus runner and inspector subsystem packages; loew-runner source and meaningful Git history/provenance are preserved in the consolidation rather than copied as anonymous files; existing Inspector/Relay history remains intact from the repository rename; package/workspace/test/build boundaries are explicit; night shift is represented as a Relay feature/view, not another product; no production routing or old repository deletion occurs yet; exact source and history import are independently verifiable before Batch 3.
queue.next_action: Start only after Batch 1 is merged and verified. Import history/code first, then normalize package boundaries without rewriting provenance.

queue.goal: Batch 3: migrate durable coordination, QA, Visuals and operation authority into Relay so the canonical managed project/control identity becomes relay and the MCP no longer depends on a separate loew-runner repository.
queue.acceptance: Canonical managed project id is relay; current active/held/completed coordination history, queued roadmap, QA helper contracts, Visuals identity and publication/operation receipts are migrated without loss or duplication; runner remains an internal coordination engine rather than a separate product/repo; inspector remains an internal verification/evidence engine; Relay MCP runner-control tools read/write the new canonical state and preserve exact-head/readback safety; old loew-runner/loew-inspector ids are no longer required for active control; stale pre-consolidation queued work is explicitly migrated or marked superseded rather than remaining actionable.
queue.next_action: Start after Batch 2 history/package import is verified. Migrate state with before/after manifests and exact-count/readback checks before switching MCP authority.

queue.goal: Batch 4: ship one Relay experience across web and in-chat MCP UI, with runner and inspector exposed as capabilities rather than separate applications and night shift as the while-you-were-away view.
queue.acceptance: Relay web and in-chat MCP surfaces consume the same durable state/receipt model; web navigation centers on human jobs such as Today, Projects, Review, Automations/operations and Night Shift rather than subsystem branding; visual review, screenshots/video/live preview, QA questions/checklists/notes/verdicts live inside Relay; runner and inspector may appear in technical details but not as separate products users must navigate to; no separate Runner/Inspector dashboard is required; deep links preserve project/operation/review context; mobile/desktop and full-screen review are usable; deterministic checks remain agent-owned.
queue.next_action: Start after Batch 3 makes Relay the canonical state authority. Reuse the merged operator/QA work instead of redesigning from zero.

queue.goal: Batch 5: create and cut production over to the canonical Relay Worker/runtime at relay.loew.fi while preserving useful Cloudflare infrastructure and proving MCP/web continuity before any destructive cleanup.
queue.acceptance: Canonical Worker/script identity is relay and exact merged Relay source is deployed to it; relay.loew.fi serves the unified web app and /mcp endpoint; existing useful secrets, Browser binding, R2 data/binding, account identity and Access policy/application are preserved or retargeted instead of needlessly recreated; Access/OAuth/self-hosted-domain/callback metadata points at relay.loew.fi only where product routing is concerned; Cloudflare write allowlists and deployment annotations use relay; the full MCP tool/resource/skill surface, web app, GitHub operations, QA/evidence and release flows are verified on the new runtime; old scripts/domains remain untouched until verification is complete.
queue.next_action: Start after Batch 4 exact-head merge. Create/deploy the new Relay runtime, retarget Access and hostname bindings, then run end-to-end verification. Do not delete legacy resources in this batch.

queue.goal: Batch 6: remove the old product identities and legacy runtime surfaces after Relay has passed end-to-end production verification.
queue.acceptance: runner.loew.fi, inspector.loew.fi and relay-inspector.loew.fi are removed from active Cloudflare custom domains/routes and Access application domain lists; old loew-inspector/loew-runner Worker or gateway identities are deleted or renamed when no longer required; obsolete Inspector/Runner-specific Access apps/policies are removed or consolidated while reusable underlying credentials/storage remain intact; loew-runner repository is retired only after its source/history/state import is proven complete; no active config, registry, MCP receipt, workflow, docs or UI requires loew-runner or loew-inspector ids; old queued assignments are closed/superseded; relay.loew.fi and lrnolivia/relay are the only canonical product surfaces. Platform-managed GitHub rename redirects may exist, but Relay does not reference or depend on them.
queue.next_action: Run only after Batch 5 production proof is complete and rollback is known-good. Inventory every legacy reference/resource, remove in dependency order, and finish with a clean search/readback plus live MCP/web verification.
